summary: Lolo NF site 11 miles south of Missoula; its 1957 tower moved to Blue Mountain in 1966 and still stands there; no source describes Davis Point today.

facts.status_note: The tower and cab were moved to Blue Mountain in 1966; no source read describes the Davis Point site today

access.note: No source read describes the Davis Point site today; the relocated tower at Blue Mountain is described as heavily visited

events.note: November 1944 Independent Record item: Davis Point selected for a new model lookout; gives 20 miles south of Missoula by road
January 1946 item: new model lookout described as being completed, with a 40-foot creosote-treated tower and 14x14 cab, for use the next fire season
41-foot treated timber tower erected at Davis Point; the 1946 article does not say whether the 1946 structure was the one erected or was replaced
Tower and cab moved to Blue Mountain southwest of Missoula; the Blue Mountain register entry gives the same move

notes_for_editor: Distance conflicts: the 1944 item says 20 miles south of Missoula by road; firelookout.com says 11 miles south. Both are reported in the story. Chronology gap: the January 1946 item says the model was being completed, and the 1957 entries say a new 41-foot tower was erected; no source read says how the two relate. Height: the record's height_m 12.2 (40 ft) matches the 1946 design, while the 1957 structure is 41 ft per both lookout pages; not changed. Elevation: firelookout.com gives 5699 ft for Davis Point. Blue Mountain figures differ between sources (firelookout.com 6460 ft; NHLR 6,366 ft; cab 14x14 in the 1946 plan, 15x15 in the NHLR entry); the Blue Mountain record (us-mt-blue-mountain-lolo-nf) should carry its own story. The filming claim in the NHLR entry was not checked elsewhere. A web search found no description of the Davis Point site today.
